newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Costain chief sees debt wipeout.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Costain chief sees debt wipeout.

text.p: Costain Group, the loss-making British engineering and construction firm, would be in a position to wipe out most of its debts estimated at more than 38 million stg by next January, chief executive Alan Lovell said.
The group announced asset sales of 52 million stg and top management changes as part of plans to focus its resources in its core construction and engineering business.

Costain earlier said it would sell its U.S. Coal division to Rencoal of the U.S. for 28.6 million stg and its one-third stake in the London Spitalfields development site to Malaysia's Metacorp for 23.4 million stg.
"The sale will help us to wipe out a net debt position of 38 million stg as on October end," Lovell told Reuters.
"We are getting rid of our dead wood. There will be no more sales, the restructuring is over," he said.

Costain reported half-year losses of 19.2 million stg in the six months to June 30 and Lovell declined to forecast full-year results or when the company would return to profit but said 1997 "was crucial".
However, he said the group was doing "profitably" in its construction and civil engineering businesses.
Lovell is to step down as chief executive but remains in place until a successor has been appointed.
Lovell did not rule out a possible appointment from outside the company. "I am looking at several candidates... in and out", he said.
The company's chairman Christopher Benson is also stepping down to be replaced by current deputy chairman Azman Firdaus bin Shafii.
Lovell said the group had also arranged for new short-term facilities from UK banks which would continue until mid-June but he declined to specify the terms of the facility.
A part of this bank facility would also be used to meet the costs of litigation linked to a U.S. gold mine.
Costain has focused its future strategy firmly on southeast Asia and the Middle East and its shareholder base reflects this.
The company's three biggest shareholders are Intria of Malaysia ACID.KL, M A Kharafi and Sons of Kuwait and Raymond International of Saudi Arabia.

It announced today that it has conditional option agreements with Indonesian industrialist Hendri Luhur and the Kuwaiti Kharafi family for them to suscribe to 13.4 million new shares at 40-50 pence each for a total 5.4 million stg between March 1 and June 30 1997. Luhur would become a new shareholder in the group.
Lovell said the group expected to conclude a 750 million stg bridge contract in Penang in a joint deal with Luhur.
He said Costain expected big, long-term construction contracts in southeast Asia, currently witnessing a spate of industrial reforms.
He expected his company's shares to relist on the London Stock Exchange once the sale of U.S. Coal was over, likely by the end of December, although Lovell said it could take until January.
